title: Identity-open normalization and domains of the closed exceptional Hom chain
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $R=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$, $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, and $\eta:1\to U_TS_T$ for the specified comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; $S_T$ is the exact derived pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Put $F=i_*^{\mathrm{et}}$, $Q=i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}$, and let $F\dashv I$ be the ordinary etale exceptional adjunction [lem-exc-closed-ambient], with bijection $\beta_{L,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(FL,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,IN)$. Identify the etale compact-support adjoint for $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$ with $I$ by the counit-compatible adjunction comparison, and put $J=S_ZIU_P$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Equip $J$ with the specified relative Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for $c$. Let $H\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ with $IH\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$.

Then $IU_PS_PH$ is bounded below, $\alpha_H=S_ZI(\eta_H):S_ZIH\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_PH$ is an isomorphism, and $(IH,\alpha_H)$ is a bounded-below etale-origin witness for $JS_PH$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. For every $L\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$, under the canonical identity-open identifications, the canonical compact-support comparison $QS_ZL\to S_PFL$ of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] is $\delta_L^{-1}$, where $\delta_L:S_PFL\xrightarrow{\sim}QS_ZL$ is the named counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The specified relative bijection at the identity witness for $S_ZL$ is exactly the following composite, not merely an unspecified bijection between its endpoints:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Phi_{L,H}:\operatorname{Hom}(QS_ZL,S_PH)&\xrightarrow{g\mapsto g\circ\delta_L}\operatorname{Hom}(S_PFL,S_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{a\mapsto U_P(a)\circ\eta_{FL}}\operatorname{Hom}(FL,U_PS_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{L,U_PS_PH}}\operatorname{Hom}(L,IU_PS_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{S_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(S_ZL,JS_PH).
\end{aligned}$$

proof.text: Specialize openImmersionLowerShriekComparison_coherence to the identity open. Descend the equation with mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, its whiskering compatibility and the derived composition unit laws. The resulting equation is o;t_pro = S_Z(t_et). Naturality of the inverse direct-image comparison at t_et moves S_P F(t_et) to Q S_Z(t_et). The identity-open factors cancel, proving the displayed inverse-mate equation.

proof.text: Expand specifiedExceptionalHomEquiv at the identity witness; the witness factors become identities. Invert the previous comparison equation to obtain C^{-1};q = S_P(e);delta. For adjc and beta, naturality of their rightAdjointUniq comparison and its unit equation identify adjc.homEquiv(f);r with beta.homEquiv(e^{-1};f). Apply S_Z, use naturality of the comparison adjunction in the left variable, and cancel e^{-1};e. This is exactly the stated four-factor Hom formula.
